questions.question_text: Compare the Organised and Unorganised employment sectors across three key features: job security, working hours, and social security benefits.
questions.correct_answer: Organised: Formal appointment, job security, fixed hours with overtime pay, statutory provident fund, paid leave, and medical benefits. Unorganised: Informal hiring, no job security (fired anytime), long unregulated hours without extra pay, and zero paid leave or social security.
questions.explanation: Organised enterprises are registered under labor laws; unorganised units operate outside regulatory oversight, leaving workers vulnerable.

questions.question_text: Illustrate sectoral interdependence by describing how a strike by cotton transport truck drivers impacts both a textile factory (Secondary) and a retail clothing store (Tertiary).
questions.correct_answer: If truck drivers strike, raw cotton cannot reach the textile factory, halting Secondary manufacturing. Consequently, finished garments cannot reach retail stores, crippling Tertiary sales and causing revenue losses across all sectors.
questions.explanation: The Tertiary sector provides essential logistical linkages; disruptions in transport stall physical production and commercial distribution simultaneously.
questions.hint_modal: Hint: Focus on the core definition of interdependence in chapter 2.

questions.question_text: India experienced a major GDP structural shift toward the Tertiary sector post-1970s, yet employment did not shift proportionally out of Agriculture. Explain the underlying structural cause.
questions.correct_answer: Industrial and service sectors failed to generate sufficient employment opportunities despite high GDP output growth. Service sector expansion relied heavily on capital-intensive IT and finance jobs requiring high skills, leaving unskilled rural labor trapped in smallholder farming.
questions.explanation: Growth in GDP was jobless/skill-intensive, causing a mismatch where over 44% of workers remained in low-productivity agriculture.

questions.question_text: Case Study: Laxmi owns 2 hectares of unirrigated land worked by all 5 family members. Even if 2 members leave to work on a canal construction site, total farm output remains unchanged. Identify the economic phenomenon and recommend two policy measures.
questions.correct_answer: Phenomenon: Disguised Unemployment (Underemployment), where marginal labor productivity is zero. Policy measures: (1) Provide subsidized micro-irrigation credit to enable multi-cropping; (2) Establish local agro-processing industries to absorb surplus farm labor.
questions.explanation: Removing disguised workers reveals hidden surplus labor; irrigation and rural enterprise diversification convert underemployed workers into productive earners.
questions.hint_modal: Hint: Focus on the core definition of Laxmi in chapter 2.
